findings.reason: The protected app-local and Accepted native sources perform the direct iterative DFS: each reachable node is popped once, its child references are swapped in place, and each existing child is scheduled once. The implementation is clear, conventional, O(n)-time, and O(n)-space in the worst case, so no candidate is justified.

The former capacity-unit tiers were off by one and its 255-node largest tree exceeded the source maximum of 100 nodes. A scaling control is also unnecessary because changing every node's child orientation imposes Omega(n) work. A verified asymptotic-optimality certificate now proves matching Omega(n) and O(n) bounds.

The local-swap reachability argument and explicit-stack bounds already match both protected forms. Alternatives and structural boundaries now use explicit labels, and the Optimal summary states the exact in-place DFS behavior.
